#### Load the libraries

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(quantmod)
library(readr)
library(knitr)
```

#### Identify stocks common to both years

We use a publicly available reconstruction of past S&P 500 membership. We cross the membership snapshots in the beginning of 2020 and 2025. This is not to say that membership has to be maintained for both years


```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Read the historical membership file
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chinobing/historical_sp500_constituents/main/sp_500_historical_components.csv"

membership <- read_csv(url, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), show_col_types = FALSE)

# Convert dates and put them in chronological order
membership$date <- as.Date(membership$date)
membership <- membership[!is.na(membership$date), ]
membership <- membership[order(membership$date), ]

# Get the most recent membership list on or before a date
get_members <- function(date) {
  date <- as.Date(date)
  rows <- which(membership$date <= date)

  if (length(rows) == 0) {
    stop("No membership snapshot available")
  }

  i <- tail(rows, 1)

  # Check that the snapshot is no more than 31 days old
  if (as.numeric(date - membership$date[i]) > 31) {
    stop("The available membership snapshot is too old")
  }

  cat("Snapshot used:", as.character(membership$date[i]), "\n")

  # Makes stock label into a vector
  trimws(strsplit(membership$tickers[i], ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
}

# Get membership lists for the beginning of each year
members2020 <- get_members("2020-01-01")
members2025 <- get_members("2025-01-01")

# Keep stocks appearing in both lists
stocks <- sort(intersect(members2020, members2025))

# Replace dots with hyphens for Yahoo ticker symbols
stocks <- unique(gsub(".", "-", stocks, fixed = TRUE))

cat("Stock series:", length(stocks), "\n")
```

#### Download prices and calculate returns

We use the adjusted-close field from Yahoo. The observations of the previous December allow us to compute the initial return in each year. Excludes stocks with incomplete or incorrect histories

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Download adjusted prices for one stock and year
download_prices <- function(stock, year) {
  prices <- getSymbols(
    stock,
    src = "yahoo",
    from = paste0(year - 1, "-12-20"),
    to = paste0(year + 1, "-01-01"),
    auto.assign = FALSE
  )

  Ad(prices)
}

# Use SPY only to identify the reference trading dates
calendar2020 <- download_prices("SPY", 2020)
calendar2025 <- download_prices("SPY", 2025)

dates2020 <- as.Date(zoo::index(calendar2020))
dates2025 <- as.Date(zoo::index(calendar2025))

dates2020 <- dates2020[format(dates2020, "%Y") == "2020"]
dates2025 <- dates2025[format(dates2025, "%Y") == "2025"]

# Calculate returns
get_returns <- function(prices, dates) {
  values <- as.numeric(prices)

  if (any(!is.finite(values)) || any(values <= 0)) {
    stop("Invalid or missing adjusted prices")
  }

  returns <- diff(log(prices))
  position <- match(dates, as.Date(zoo::index(returns)))
  returns <- as.numeric(returns[position])

  if (any(!is.finite(returns))) {
    stop("Incomplete return history")
  }

  if (sd(returns) == 0) {
    stop("Zero return variance")
  }

  returns
}

# Store the returns
returns2020 <- list()
returns2025 <- list()

excluded <- data.frame(
  Stock = character(),
  Reason = character()
)

for (i in seq_along(stocks)) {
  stock <- stocks[i]
  
  result <- tryCatch({
    prices2020 <- download_prices(stock, 2020)
    prices2025 <- download_prices(stock, 2025)

    list(
      year2020 = get_returns(prices2020, dates2020),
      year2025 = get_returns(prices2025, dates2025)
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    conditionMessage(e)
  })

  if (is.list(result)) {
    returns2020[[stock]] <- result$year2020
    returns2025[[stock]] <- result$year2025
  } else {
    excluded <- rbind(
      excluded,
      data.frame(Stock = stock, Reason = result)
    )
  }

  Sys.sleep(0.3)
}

if (length(returns2020) < 10) {
  stop("Too few stocks were downloaded successfully")
}

# Rows are trading days and columns are individual stocks
R2020 <- do.call(cbind, returns2020)
R2025 <- do.call(cbind, returns2025)

data2020 <- data.frame(
  date = dates2020,
  R2020,
  check.names = FALSE
)

data2025 <- data.frame(
  date = dates2025,
  R2025,
  check.names = FALSE
)

stopifnot(identical(colnames(R2020), colnames(R2025)))

kable(
  data.frame(
    Year = c(2020, 2025),
    Trading_days = c(nrow(R2020), nrow(R2025)),
    Stocks = c(ncol(R2020), ncol(R2025))
  ),
  caption = "Retained stock-return data"
)

kable(excluded, caption = "Excluded stock series")
```

#### Center and scale the returns

We subtract the yearly mean for each stock and use the same pooled standard deviation throughout the two years

```{r}
# Subtract each stock's average return within each year
C2020 <- scale(R2020, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
C2025 <- scale(R2025, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)

# Calculate one pooled standard deviation for each stock
pooled_sd <- sqrt(
  (colSums(C2020^2) + colSums(C2025^2)) /
    (nrow(C2020) + nrow(C2025) - 2)
)

# Check that every standard deviation is finite and positive
stopifnot(
  all(is.finite(pooled_sd)),
  all(pooled_sd > 0)
)

# Divide each stock's centered returns by its pooled standard deviation
X2020 <- sweep(C2020, 2, pooled_sd, "/")
X2025 <- sweep(C2025, 2, pooled_sd, "/")
```

#### Principal component analysis

PCA uses all available observations each year
Differences in explained variance do not by se imply different loading spaces

```{r}
# Run PCA on the already centered and scaled returns
pca2020 <- prcomp(X2020, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE)
pca2025 <- prcomp(X2025, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE)

# Square the standard deviations to get component variances
variance2020 <- pca2020$sdev^2
variance2025 <- pca2025$sdev^2

# Divide by total variance to get the proportion explained
pve2020 <- variance2020 / sum(variance2020)
pve2025 <- variance2025 / sum(variance2025)

# Summarize the first ten components
# Cumulative percentages add the contributions up to each component
pca_table <- data.frame(
  PC = 1:10,
  Percent_2020 = 100 * pve2020[1:10],
  Percent_2025 = 100 * pve2025[1:10],
  Cumulative_2020 = 100 * cumsum(pve2020)[1:10],
  Cumulative_2025 = 100 * cumsum(pve2025)[1:10]
)

kable(pca_table, digits = 3)

# Summarize the first component and the first three together
presentation_table <- data.frame(
  Component = c(
    "First principal component",
    "First three principal components"
  ),
  Percent_2020 = 100 * c(pve2020[1], sum(pve2020[1:3])),
  Percent_2025 = 100 * c(pve2025[1], sum(pve2025[1:3]))
)

kable(presentation_table, digits = 3)

# Plot both years using the same axes
matplot(
  1:10,
  100 * cbind(pve2020[1:10], pve2025[1:10]),
  type = "b",
  pch = c(16, 17),
  lty = 1,
  col = c("navy", "darkorange"),
  xlab = "Principal component",
  ylab = "Variance explained (%)"
)

# Identify each year's line
legend(
  "topright",
  legend = c("2020", "2025"),
  col = c("navy", "darkorange"),
  pch = c(16, 17),
  lty = 1
)
```

#### Prepare equal sample sizes

For the midpoint test, we save the first $T$ observations in each year, where $T$ is the maximum possible even sample size
This corresponds to sample sizes, not calendar dates

```{r}
# Find the smaller number of observations across the two years
T <- min(nrow(X2020), nrow(X2025))

# Round down to an even number for the midpoint split
T <- 2 * floor(T / 2)

# Keep the first T observations and subtract each column's mean
A <- scale(X2020[1:T, ], center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
B <- scale(X2025[1:T, ], center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)

# Display the sample size and date range used for each year
sample_table <- data.frame(
  Year = c(2020, 2025),
  Test_observations = T,
  Stocks = ncol(A),
  First_date = c(dates2020[1], dates2025[1]),
  Last_date = c(dates2020[T], dates2025[T])
)

kable(sample_table)
```

#### Estimate the loading matrices

We provide a three-factor specification
The loading entries themselves cannot be directly compared, since the factor representation is known only up to transformation

```{r}
# Choose three factors
r <- 3

# Calculate the PCA decompositions using SVD
pca_A <- svd(A, nu = r, nv = 0)
pca_B <- svd(B, nu = r, nv = 0)

# Keep the first three factor directions
U2020 <- pca_A$u[, 1:r, drop = FALSE]
U2025 <- pca_B$u[, 1:r, drop = FALSE]

# Normalize the factors so their sample second-moment matrix is the identity
F2020 <- sqrt(T) * U2020
F2025 <- sqrt(T) * U2025

# Estimate how each stock relates to the factors
Lambda2020 <- t(A) %*% F2020 / T
Lambda2025 <- t(B) %*% F2025 / T

# Display the estimated loadings for the first five stocks
loading_table <- data.frame(
  Stock = colnames(A)[1:5],
  Lambda2020[1:5, ],
  Lambda2025[1:5, ]
)

# Label the columns by year and factor
names(loading_table) <- c(
  "Stock",
  "2020 Factor 1", "2020 Factor 2", "2020 Factor 3",
  "2025 Factor 1", "2025 Factor 2", "2025 Factor 3"
)

kable(loading_table, digits = 3)
```

#### Define the transformation and Wald test

This function corrects the factor count of original and transformed series to satisfy the previous presentation requirement. It does not use Bai-Ng factor selection

```{r}
common_structure_test <- function(A, B, r, bandwidth) {

  T <- nrow(B)

  # Check equal sample sizes and matching stock columns
  stopifnot(
    nrow(A) == T,
    T %% 2 == 0,
    identical(colnames(A), colnames(B)),
    bandwidth >= 1,
    bandwidth < T,
    bandwidth == floor(bandwidth)
  )

  # Calculate PCA decompositions for the original datasets
  pca_A <- svd(A, nu = 0, nv = r)
  pca_B <- svd(B, nu = 0, nv = r)

  # Keep orthonormal bases for the loading spaces
  Q1 <- pca_A$v[, 1:r, drop = FALSE]
  Q2 <- pca_B$v[, 1:r, drop = FALSE]

  # Split Dataset B into equal halves
  first <- 1:(T / 2)
  second <- (T / 2 + 1):T

  B_first <- B[first, , drop = FALSE]
  B_second <- B[second, , drop = FALSE]

  # Project each half onto its corresponding loading space
  projected_first <- B_first %*% Q1 %*% t(Q1)
  projected_second <- B_second %*% Q2 %*% t(Q2)

  # Average the original and projected observations
  Y <- B
  Y[first, ] <- (B_first + projected_first) / 2
  Y[second, ] <- (B_second + projected_second) / 2

  # Estimate and normalize exactly r factors from the transformed data
  pca_Y <- svd(Y, nu = r, nv = 0)
  Fhat <- sqrt(T) * pca_Y$u[, 1:r, drop = FALSE]

  # Identify the lower triangle including the diagonal
  lower <- lower.tri(matrix(0, r, r), diag = TRUE)
  df <- r * (r + 1) / 2

  # Store the nonduplicated factor products for each observation
  products <- matrix(0, nrow = T, ncol = df)

  for (i in 1:T) {
    factor_product <- tcrossprod(Fhat[i, ])
    products[i, ] <- factor_product[lower]
  }

  # Compare factor second moments between the two halves
  first_sum <- colSums(products[first, , drop = FALSE])
  second_sum <- colSums(products[second, , drop = FALSE])

  V <- (first_sum - second_sum) / sqrt(T)

  # Subtract the corresponding entries of the identity matrix
  identity_entries <- diag(r)[lower]
  Z <- sweep(products, 2, identity_entries, "-")

  # Calculate the lag-zero covariance
  Omega <- crossprod(Z) / T

  # Add lagged covariances with Bartlett weights
  if (bandwidth > 1) {
    for (lag in 1:(bandwidth - 1)) {

      current <- Z[(lag + 1):T, , drop = FALSE]
      previous <- Z[1:(T - lag), , drop = FALSE]

      Gamma <- crossprod(current, previous) / T
      weight <- 1 - lag / bandwidth

      Omega <- Omega + weight * (Gamma + t(Gamma))
    }
  }

  # Remove small numerical asymmetries
  Omega <- (Omega + t(Omega)) / 2

  # Stop if the covariance cannot be reliably inverted
  if (rcond(Omega) < 1e-10) {
    stop("The estimated long-run covariance is nearly singular")
  }

  # Calculate the Wald statistic and chi-square p-value
  W <- as.numeric(t(V) %*% solve(Omega, V))
  p_value <- pchisq(W, df = df, lower.tail = FALSE)

  # Return the test results
  data.frame(
    r = r,
    bandwidth = bandwidth,
    W = W,
    df = df,
    p_value = p_value
  )
}
```

#### Calculate the presentation specification

We use three factors, bandwidth seven, and transform the 2025 series

```{r}
# Set the significance level
alpha <- 0.05

# Test using three factors and bandwidth six
# A contains 2020 returns and B contains 2025 returns
# The function transforms B
main_result <- common_structure_test(
  A, B,
  r = 3,
  bandwidth = 7
)

# Calculate the chi-square rejection threshold
main_result$critical_value <- qchisq(
  1 - alpha,
  df = main_result$df
)

# Reject the null when the p-value is below alpha
main_result$conclusion <- ifelse(
  main_result$p_value < alpha,
  "Reject H0",
  "Do not reject H0"
)

# Display the results
kable(
  main_result,
  digits = 6,
  caption = "Three factors and bandwidth six with 2025 transformed"
)
```
